narration: Welcome to the Bronze Gallery. Here we have the Chola bronze sculpture “Krishna Subduing the Serpent Kaliya,” accession number NM 60.5/2, dating from the 12th century CE and crafted in Tamil Nadu. The 52‑centimetre figure captures the moment Krishna, in a graceful dance, pulls up the tail of the poisonous serpent Kaliya, illustrating the Bhagavata Purana tale of Krishna protecting Vrindavan’s villagers. This piece is part of our Chola bronze collection, paired thematically with the Nataraja, both celebrating the cosmic dance that vanquishes evil and maintains universal rhythm.
